name: kit_a4_v1
_about: The one layout spec of the kitting task: the printed sheet (paper, markers, target cells, start spots), the object classes and which object goes where. tasks/kitting/spec.py reads it; sheet.py prints it; sim/kitting_scene.py builds the twin from it; locate.py finds it in a camera image.

Units: mm. Sheet frame: origin = centre of the page, +x = towards the right edge of the printed page (landscape, text upright), +y = towards the top edge, z out of the paper. Laid on the table with its BOTTOM edge towards the arm base (sheet +y = arm forward at sheet yaw 0).

Start spots: where the human puts each object before a run (outline printed on the sheet, long axis drawn). At 299x224 the overview camera cannot localise a 4 mm screw (about 1.3 px wide at 0.45 m), so object positions come from the located sheet: pose(object) = pose(sheet) * pose(spot). See docs/kitting/README.md.

markers._about: ids 10..13 (the table already uses 20..23). 50 mm is the largest that fits the corners: at the sheet's distance (0.35..0.55 m) the overview camera sees ~15 x 10 px per marker, enough for perception/aruco.detect (3x upscaled). Centres 6 mm + half a marker in from the page edges (printers keep ~4 mm margins).

grid._about: 3 columns x 2 rows of target cells in the top (far) half, the same for the start spots in the bottom (near) half. Column pitch 60 mm keeps the open jaws (outer width ~73 mm) clear of neighbours by ~8 mm; 42 mm cells leave ~6 mm around a 30 mm cap.

screw._about: M4 x 25 pan-head steel screw lying on its side; long axis = sheet x at spot yaw 0 (head towards -x). Mass: steel 7.85 g/cm3 x 0.42 cm3.

cap._about: PET bottle cap (28 mm neck finish), closed side up; 2.5 g weighed caps are 2-3 g. Modelled solid (contact is the same).

box._about: small plastic parts box 30 x 20 x 15 mm; long side = sheet x at spot yaw 0. 6 g.

placement._about: Nominal pose of the sheet centre in the arm base frame (sim frame: +y = arm forward, +x = the arm's right) and the training randomization. Far cells reach 0.32 m, near spots 0.17 m from the base: inside the comfortable radius (profile workspace.comfortable_radius 0.35).

human_placement._about: how well a person puts an object on its printed spot (assumed, not measured)
